# Peace of Mind Planning Session — Checklist

<!-- Generated by `npm run design:forms`. Edit lib/designMeeting/formSpec.ts, not this file. -->

The order to run a Peace of Mind Planning Session, and what each section has to come away
with. It gathers the facts the Estate Plan Proposal and the Massachusetts estate-tax
worksheet need, and the first version of the plan. Provisions wait for the design meeting.

## Before the meeting

- [ ] Read the intake questionnaire and the lead's notes; do not re-ask what they answer.
- [ ] Run **PMPS Proposal Preflight** in the Assistant on the lead so the gaps are known
      before the client arrives.
- [ ] Start Granola with the PMPS template, or print the PMPS worksheet.

## During the meeting

### 1. Clients

Full legal names as they should appear on the documents. Citizenship and county are not optional.

- [ ] Client name
- [ ] Client date of birth
- [ ] Client citizenship — US Citizen / Permanent Resident / Non-Resident Alien / Non-US — status unconfirmed
- [ ] Client phone
- [ ] Client email
- [ ] Marital status — single / married / divorced / widowed / separated / domestic_partner / civil_union / unmarried_partnership
- [ ] Spouse name
- [ ] Spouse date of birth
- [ ] Spouse citizenship — US Citizen / Permanent Resident / Non-Resident Alien / Non-US — status unconfirmed
- [ ] Marriage date
- [ ] Street
- [ ] City
- [ ] State
- [ ] ZIP
- [ ] County — Barnstable / Berkshire / Bristol / Dukes / Essex / Franklin / Hampden / Hampshire / Middlesex / Nantucket / Norfolk / Plymouth / Suffolk / Worcester
- [ ] Disabled veteran
- [ ] First name each client goes by

### 2. Family

Every child by full legal name and exact date of birth. A birth year alone is not enough.

- [ ] Children
- [ ] Child from a prior relationship
- [ ] Child with special needs or receiving benefits
- [ ] Deceased child with descendants
- [ ] Anyone the client intends to leave out, and why

### 3. Assets & Estate Tax

Every line needs a number. A blank is not zero — it stops the estate-tax worksheet reconciling.

- [ ] Assets
- [ ] Real property (address, value, mortgage balance, how titled; flag anything outside Massachusetts)
- [ ] Bank and brokerage accounts (institution, approximate value, owner)
- [ ] Retirement accounts (type, institution, value, current beneficiary)
- [ ] Life insurance (carrier, death benefit, term or whole, who OWNS the policy, beneficiary)
- [ ] Business interests (entity, percent owned, valuation basis)
- [ ] Other assets (vehicles, digital assets, collectibles, money owed to the client)
- [ ] Are these values per spouse or combined
- [ ] Prior taxable gifts
- [ ] Anticipated inheritance (source and expected amount)

### 4. Goals & Concerns

In the client’s own words. This is what the proposal is written to.

- [ ] Goals notes
- [ ] Concerns
- [ ] What prompted the call now
- [ ] Asset-protection worries (divorce, creditors, a spendthrift beneficiary)
- [ ] Incapacity or long-term-care worries
- [ ] Pets (name, and who would care for them)

### 5. Proposed Plan

The recommendation made at the table. Mark anything the client has not agreed to as "not decided".

- [ ] Plan type — pour_over / outright_will / testamentary_trust
- [ ] Joint plan
- [ ] Residual beneficiary method — outright / staggered / trust_for_life / custom
- [ ] Distribution age
- [ ] First stagger age
- [ ] First stagger percentage
- [ ] Second stagger age
- [ ] Second stagger percentage
- [ ] Final stagger age
- [ ] Joint trust or separate mirror trusts
- [ ] Credit-shelter / bypass planning discussed
- [ ] Discretionary standard before distribution ages (HEMS; is college called out)
- [ ] Contingent beneficiaries if a child predeceases (full legal names)

### 6. Fiduciaries (first thoughts)

Who the client has in mind. These are confirmed at the design meeting, not here.

- [ ] Spouses serve as co-trustees
- [ ] Trustee — primary
- [ ] Trustee — alternate
- [ ] Trustee — second alternate
- [ ] Personal representative — primary
- [ ] Personal representative — alternate
- [ ] Attorney-in-fact (financial POA) — primary
- [ ] Attorney-in-fact (financial POA) — alternate
- [ ] Health care agent — primary
- [ ] Health care agent — alternate
- [ ] Guardian for minor children — primary
- [ ] Guardian for minor children — alternate
- [ ] Any fiduciary outside the U.S., named as a couple, or under about 25

### 7. Engagement & Next Steps

What the client was quoted and what happens next.

- [ ] Drafting notes
- [ ] Legal plan (MetLife / ARAG / LegalShield / none) and member ID
- [ ] Flat fee quoted, and what it covers
- [ ] Optional services discussed (real property transfer, advanced estate-tax planning, supervised signing)
- [ ] Engagement decision (hired / thinking it over / not proceeding)
- [ ] Documents the client will send (deeds, statements, existing plan, beneficiary forms)
- [ ] Design meeting date

## After the meeting

- [ ] Run the **PMPS recipe** in Granola. Attach its recap to the lead with
      **Add meeting notes**.
- [ ] Work the recipe's **Missing information** list into the follow-up email — every
      asset line still without a number, and every policy without an owner.
- [ ] Once the matter is hired, open `/admin/drafting/<matterId>` and paste the recap
      above **Missing information** into **Complete sheet → Paste notes**, or upload the
      worksheet through **Complete sheet → Word document**.
- [ ] Review and accept, then use **Create follow-up task** in the same dialog to turn what
      the sheet still lacks into a checklist task on the matter.
- [ ] Billing (legal plan, fee quoted) has no design-sheet field. Record it on the matter;
      the import carries it only as drafting notes.
